title: Website Technology Stack Detector
description: Give it domains or URLs; get the technologies each site uses, with the evidence for every detection. Plain HTTP scan by default; browser rendering is optional and costs more.

urls.title: URLs or domains
urls.description: Bulk input: one domain or URL per line, up to 10,000. Plain domains (example.com) and full URLs are accepted; https:// is assumed when missing; duplicates are removed. Each site is fetched once.

browserFallback.title: Browser fallback for JavaScript-only pages (optional, slower, higher price)
browserFallback.sectionDescription: The default is a plain HTTP scan: one page request plus DNS and TLS lookups, typically 2–4 seconds per site. Browser rendering is optional and changes speed and price.
browserFallback.description: OFF by default. When ON, a page that returns only a thin JavaScript shell (little visible text after a plain request) is re-rendered in headless Chromium so runtime-loaded technologies become visible. This makes those pages take roughly 10–30 seconds instead of 2–4 seconds and bills them as a Full scan instead of a Basic scan. Pages that do not need it stay Basic. Blocked pages are never retried in a browser.

alwaysUseBrowser.title: Render every page in a browser (slowest, highest price)
alwaysUseBrowser.description: OFF by default. Renders every reachable page in headless Chromium to catch tags injected after page load (for example analytics loaded through a tag manager). Roughly 10–30 seconds per page, at most 2 pages at a time, and every successfully rendered page is billed as a Full scan. If the browser step fails on a site, its plain-HTTP result is returned, billed as Basic, and `browserError` explains why. Blocked pages are never retried or bypassed.

respectRobotsTxt.title: Respect robots.txt
respectRobotsTxt.description: ON by default and recommended. Before scanning a site the Actor reads its /robots.txt (once per host) and skips the page if the rules disallow it for this Actor's user agent (TechStackDetector) or for all bots. Skipped pages are reported as `skipped_robots` and are not billed. A missing robots.txt (4xx) allows scanning; a server error (5xx) is treated as disallow, as in RFC 9309. Turn this OFF only for sites you own or have permission to scan; you are responsible for that choice.

maxConcurrency.title: Max concurrency
maxConcurrency.description: How many websites are scanned in parallel. Requests to the same host are never sent in parallel. Browser rendering is capped at 2 pages at a time regardless of this value.

timeoutSecs.title: Timeout per website (seconds)
timeoutSecs.description: Time limit for each website's page request. Sites that do not answer in time are reported as `timeout` and are not billed.

includeDns.title: Include DNS lookups
includeDns.description: Resolve A/AAAA/CNAME, name servers, MX and SPF records. Used to detect the DNS provider, the mailbox provider (from MX) and email services authorized in SPF. An SPF entry only shows that a service may send mail for the domain, so it is reported with low confidence.

includeTls.title: Include TLS certificate info
includeTls.description: Read the certificate issuer, expiry and protocol. No page content is involved.

includeEvidence.title: Include evidence for each detection
includeEvidence.description: Return the exact signal (response header, meta tag, script URL, cookie name, DNS record) that led to every detection, with a strength flag (`strong` or `weak`). Turn off for smaller output.

ecommerceSignals.title: E-commerce signals (optional)
ecommerceSignals.description: OFF by default; with it off the output is unchanged. When ON, each successfully scanned page gets an extra `ecommerce` object built only from the page that was already fetched (no extra requests, no extra charge): platform, Shopify theme name / theme store id (from the public `Shopify.theme` object), shop currency, a short list of storefront apps with a concrete script signal, and payment-method hints that the page itself shows. Each value carries an `evidence` string; a value with no evidence is left out. No e-mail addresses, phone numbers or customer data are collected.

minConfidence.title: Minimum confidence
minConfidence.description: Drop detections below this confidence (1–99) from the output. 0 keeps everything. Weak inferences (for example an SPF include or a preconnect hint) never score above 60, so a value of 65–70 returns only detections backed by direct evidence.

expectedTechnologies.sectionDescription: Leave empty for a normal scan. Fill in to get pass / fail / unknown per site for technologies you expect (or forbid). The price is the same: you pay only for the scan.
expectedTechnologies.title: Expected technologies
expectedTechnologies.description: Technologies that should be on every site, using names from the supported list (case does not matter), e.g. Google Tag Manager, Cookiebot. A site gets "fail" if one is not detected, "unknown" if the page could not be scanned or the evidence is only weak.

forbiddenTechnologies.title: Forbidden technologies
forbiddenTechnologies.description: Technologies that should NOT be on the sites, e.g. Universal Analytics. A site gets "fail" if one is detected with strong evidence.
